docs.title: Our Pledge
docs.text:
We as members, contributors, and leaders pledge to make participation in our community a harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of age, body size, visible or invisible disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status, nationality, personal appearance, race, religion, or sexual identity and orientation.

We pledge to act and interact in ways that contribute to an open, welcoming, diverse, inclusive, and healthy community.

docs.title: Our Standards
docs.text:
Examples of behavior that contributes to a positive environment for our community include:

  • Demonstrating empathy and kindness toward other people
  • Being respectful of differing opinions, viewpoints, and experiences
  • Giving and gracefully accepting constructive feedback
  • Accepting responsibility and apologizing to those affected by our mistakes, and learning from the experience
  • Focusing on what is best not just for us as individuals, but for the overall community

Examples of unacceptable behavior include:

  • The use of sexualized language or imagery, and sexual attention or advances of any kind
  • Trolling, insulting or derogatory comments, and personal or political attacks
  • Public or private harassment
  • Publishing others' private information, such as a physical or email address, without their explicit permission
  • Other conduct which could reasonably be considered inappropriate in a professional setting

docs.title: Enforcement Responsibilities
docs.text:
Community leaders are responsible for clarifying and enforcing our standards of acceptable behavior and will take appropriate and fair corrective action in response to any behavior that they deem inappropriate, threatening, offensive, or harmful.

Community leaders have the right and responsibility to remove, edit, or reject comments, commits, code, wiki edits, issues, and other contributions that are not aligned to this Code of Conduct, and will communicate reasons for moderation decisions when appropriate.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: This Code of Conduct applies within all community spaces, and also applies when an individual is officially representing the community in public spaces. Examples of representing our community include using an official e-mail address, posting via an official social media account, or acting as an appointed representative at an online or offline event.

docs.title: Enforcement
docs.text:
[!IMPORTANT] Instances of abusive, harassing, or otherwise unacceptable behavior may be reported to the community leaders responsible for enforcement by contacting conduct@{{organization}}.com.

All complaints will be reviewed and investigated promptly and fairly.

All community leaders are obligated to respect the privacy and security of the reporter of any incident.

docs.title: Enforcement Guidelines
docs.text:
Community leaders will follow these Community Impact Guidelines in determining the consequences for any action they deem in violation of this Code of Conduct:

Level Community Impact Consequence 1. Correction Use of inappropriate language or other behavior deemed unprofessional or unwelcome in the community. A private, written warning from community leaders, providing clarity around the nature of the violation and an explanation of why the behavior was inappropriate. A public apology may be requested. 2. Warning A violation through a single incident or series of actions. A warning with consequences for continued behavior. No interaction with the people involved, including unsolicited interaction with those enforcing the Code of Conduct, for a specified period of time. This includes avoiding interactions in community spaces as well as external channels like social media. Violating these terms may lead to a temporary or permanent ban. 3. Temporary Ban A serious violation of community standards, including sustained inappropriate behavior. A temporary ban from any sort of interaction or public communication with the community for a specified period of time. No public or private interaction with the people involved, including unsolicited interaction with those enforcing the Code of Conduct, is allowed during this period. Violating these terms may lead to a permanent ban. 4. Permanent Ban Demonstrating a pattern of violation of community standards, including sustained inappropriate behavior, harassment of an individual, or aggression toward or disparagement of classes of individuals. A permanent ban from any sort of public interaction within the community.

docs.title: How Can I Contribute?
docs.text:
There are many ways to contribute to {{project_name}}, and not all of them involve writing code:

  • Reporting Bugs: Help us improve by submitting detailed bug reports via our issue tracker.
  • Suggesting Features: Propose new features or enhancements that could benefit the project.
  • Improving Documentation: Fix typos, add examples, or write new guides.
  • Writing Code: Fix bugs, implement features, or improve performance.
  • Helping Others: Answer questions in Discussions or issue comments.

For general questions and help, please see SUPPORT.md.

docs.title: Contributing Code
docs.text: If you are contributing code, please follow these structured steps:

docs.title: 1. Development Setup
docs.text: Before you start coding, please refer to our Development Guide (DEVELOPING.md) for detailed instructions on: - Setting up your local environment - Installing dependencies - Running the test suite - Code formatting and linting standards

docs.title: 2. Finding an Issue
docs.text:
• Look for issues tagged with good first issue or help wanted if you are a new contributor.
  • If you plan to work on a major feature, please open an issue or discussion first to talk it over with the maintainers.

docs.title: 3. Making Changes
docs.text:
1. Fork the Repository: Fork the {{project_name}} repository to your GitHub account.
  2. Create a Branch: Create a new branch from main for your work (e.g., git checkout -b feat/add-new-feature).
  3. Write Code: Implement your changes, adhering to the project's coding standards.
  4. Write Tests: Add unit tests or integration tests for your changes to ensure stability.
  5. Run Tests: Ensure all tests and linters pass locally before committing.

docs.title: 4. Committing Your Changes
docs.text:
• Write clear, concise commit messages.
  • We recommend using Conventional Commits (e.g., feat: add support for X, fix: resolve issue with Y).
  • If you are adding a new file, please include the appropriate Apache 2.0 copyright and license header at the top.

docs.title: 5. Submitting a Pull Request
docs.text:
1. Push your branch: git push origin your-branch-name.
  2. Open a Pull Request: Open a PR against the main branch of the upstream repository.
  3. Fill out the PR Template: Provide a clear description of your changes, link to any relevant issues (e.g., Closes #123), and complete any required checklists.
  4. Pass CI: Ensure all GitHub Actions CI checks pass.
  5. Review: Address any feedback from the maintainers. Once approved and checks pass, a maintainer will merge your PR.

docs.title: Running Tests
docs.text:
We maintain strict testing standards. Our tests are located in the tests/ directory and are categorized by tier.

Test Tier Directory Description Unit tests/unit/ Fast, isolated tests for individual functions and classes. Integration tests/integration/ Slower tests that verify interactions between multiple components. End-to-End tests/e2e/ Full-stack tests simulating real user workflows.

Replace the commands below with those appropriate for your language stack:

# Python (pytest)
pytest tests/unit/
pytest tests/integration/
pytest tests/         # full suite with coverage
pytest tests/ --cov=src --cov-report=xml

# Node.js (Jest)
npx jest tests/unit/
npx jest --ci --coverage

# Go
go test ./tests/unit/...
go test ./...

# Rust
cargo test --lib           # unit tests
cargo test --test '*'      # integration tests

docs.text:

  • Formatters & Linters: We enforce code quality through CI/CD pipelines. Please refer to your language-specific guidelines for setting up local linting.

[!TIP] IDE Configuration: We highly recommend configuring your editor (e.g., VSCode, IntelliJ) to format on save using the project's formatting tools. For VSCode, ensure you have the relevant extensions installed and check .vscode/settings.json if available.

docs.title: Git Workflow & Branching
docs.text:
We follow a structured branching strategy to maintain a clean git history.

  1. Branch Naming:
  2. Feature branches: feature/short-description
  3. Bug fixes: bugfix/short-description

  4. Documentation: docs/short-description

  5. Commit Messages: We encourage following Conventional Commits.

  6. feat: add new user endpoint
  7. fix: resolve crash on startup

  8. docs: update developing guide

  9. Pull Requests:

  10. Push your branch to the remote repository.
  11. Open a Pull Request against the main branch.
  12. Ensure all CI checks (tests, linters) pass.
  13. Request a review from at least one core maintainer.

docs.title: CI/CD Architecture
docs.text: This repository uses a modular, standardized GitHub Actions architecture. Workflows are divided into core lifecycle events and reusable helper templates.

docs.title: Lifecycle Workflows
docs.text: Workflow Trigger Purpose Development (development.yml) Pull Request to main Runs quality gates, security audits, unit/integration tests, and builds documentation previews. Blocks merges if checks fail. Main (main.yml) Push to main Post-merge validation. Runs unit/integration/e2e tests, quality/security checks, and updates the latest documentation. Nightly (nightly.yml) Cron (Daily 00:00 UTC) Runs extended regression tests, alpha builds, nightly documentation deployment, and deeper security analysis. Release (release.yml) Push of v*.*.* tag Performs full verification, builds immutable release packages, versioned documentation, and publishes artifacts. Weekly (weekly.yml) Cron (Sun 00:00 UTC) Conducts dependency hygiene and full test suite regression to catch configuration drift.

docs.title: PR Feedback & Cleanup
docs.text:
• Safe PR Commenting: The pr_comment.yml workflow uses workflow_run to securely post CI status comments on pull requests, circumventing write permission limits on forks.
  • Environment Cleanup: When a PR is closed or merged, development_cleanup.yml automatically removes ephemeral documentation environments and artifacts to maintain a clean workspace.

docs.title: Reusable Templates
docs.text: Our pipelines rely on modular templates located in .github/workflows/_*.yml (e.g., _tests.yml, _quality.yml, _docs.yml, _security.yml, _build_package.yml). This ensures testing granularity and linting rules remain perfectly consistent across all stages of the software lifecycle.

docs.title: Building Documentation
docs.text:
Our documentation is built using MkDocs Material. To preview documentation changes locally:

# Install docs dependencies (if not already installed)
pip install mkdocs-material

# Serve documentation on http://127.0.0.1:8000 with hot-reload
mkdocs serve

For further assistance, please refer to our SUPPORT.md.

docs.title: Reporting a Vulnerability
docs.text:
[!IMPORTANT] Please do not report security vulnerabilities through public GitHub issues, discussions, or pull requests.

If you discover a security vulnerability, please bring it to our attention right away using one of the following methods:

  1. GitHub Security Advisories (Preferred): Use the "Report a vulnerability" button on the Security tab of this repository.
  2. Email: Send your report directly to [INSERT EMAIL ADDRESS OR SECURITY CONTACT]. (Optional: Encrypt your email using our PGP key: [INSERT PGP KEY LINK/FINGERPRINT])

docs.title: What to Include in Your Report
docs.text: To help us resolve the issue quickly, please include the following information: - Type of vulnerability (e.g., XSS, SQLi, RCE, authorization bypass). - Detailed description of the vulnerability and its potential impact. - Step-by-step instructions to reproduce the issue. - Proof of Concept (PoC) code or screenshots, if available. - Environment details (e.g., version of {{project_name}}, OS, relevant configurations).

docs.title: Triage and Resolution Process
docs.text:
We will handle your report with strict confidentiality. Our process is as follows:

  1. Acknowledgment: We will respond to your report as soon as possible, usually within [INSERT NUMBER, e.g., 48] hours.
  2. Triage: We will investigate the issue and determine its validity and severity. We may contact you for further clarification.
  3. Fix: If the vulnerability is verified, we will develop and test a patch.
  4. Disclosure: We will coordinate with you to publicly disclose the vulnerability once a fix is released. We will publicly acknowledge your responsible disclosure, if you wish.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
In Scope: - Vulnerabilities within the core {{project_name}} codebase. - Security issues in our default configurations.

Out of Scope: - Volumetric Denial of Service (DoS) attacks. - Theoretical issues without a reproducible PoC. - Vulnerabilities in third-party dependencies that are not exploitable through {{project_name}}. - Missing security headers or best practices that do not lead to a direct exploit.

(Note: We currently [do/do not] operate a bug bounty program. Disclosures are greatly appreciated but are not eligible for financial rewards at this time.)

docs.title: Personal Website and Profile README: Implementation Plan
docs.text:
Status Proposed, ready to build Date 2026-11-20 Scope The personal website served from this repo, and the GitHub profile README.md at the repo root Audience The build thread that implements this, the reviewer, and Mark

This plan is written to be executed top to bottom. Sections 1 to 4 fix the decisions, sections 5 to 14 specify the design, section 15 is the phased build order with acceptance criteria, and section 17 lists the few things only Mark can do (accounts, DNS, secrets).

Where this plan names a library version, it was checked against the npm registry on 2026-11-20. The builder should still install the latest stable release within the named major and read the current docs for anything marked verify, because several of these tools move quickly.

docs.title: 1. Goals and requirement traceability
docs.text:
Every requirement from the original brief maps to a section and a build phase.

# Requirement Where it is designed Phase R1 Own and manage the code, full control to customize anything §3, §5, §6 0 R2 Easy customization without touching components §6 (config-driven) 0 to 2 R3 About me, hobbies, and work §7.1, §8 2 R4 Research papers §7.4, §8 2 R5 Blog: link out to externally hosted posts today §7.3 (externalUrl) 2 R6 Blog: self-publish on the site §7.3, §11 2 R7 Blog: sync to other blogging services §11 (syndication) 8 R8 Coding projects §7.5 2 R9 DIY and 3D printing projects §7.5, §7.7 (ModelViewer, BillOfMaterials) 2 R10 Woodworking projects §7.5, §7.7 2 R11 Photography and travel (public) §7.6, §10 4 R12 Passcode or login protected areas §9 5 to 6 R13 Host client shoot images and albums privately §9, §10 6 R14 Clients create their own collections and share them §9.5 7 R15 Database-backed customizations, generic passcode pathways §9.6, §12 5, 9 R16 Domain registered at Squarespace §13 9 R17 Profile README, since the repo is markurtz/markurtz §14 3 R18 Modern best practices and standards §4, §16 all

Non-goals for the first release: e-commerce or print sales, comments hosted on the site, a newsletter system, multi-author support, and a visual CMS. Section 15 lists these in the backlog with the hook each one would attach to.

docs.title: 2. Summary of decisions
docs.text:
These are the choices made on Mark's behalf. Each one is reversible, and the "escape hatch" column says how.

Area Decision Why Escape hatch Framework Next.js 16 App Router, React 19, TypeScript strict Matches the suggested stack. Static content pages plus server-side logic for the client area in one codebase. Avoid Vercel-only APIs so OpenNext on Cloudflare stays possible. Hosting Vercel with Git integration Preview deployment per PR, zero-config Next.js. See the Hobby plan caveat in §13.4. Content engine Velite (not Contentlayer) Contentlayer is unmaintained. Velite was on the shortlist, is bundler independent (works with Turbopack), uses Zod schemas, and emits typed JSON. All access goes through src/lib/content/, so swapping to Content Collections touches one folder. Styling Tailwind CSS v4, shadcn/ui components copied into the repo, CSS variable theme tokens Owned code, no component library lock-in, theme changes in one file. Components are plain files. Database Supabase Postgres, accessed server-side only through Drizzle ORM Typed queries, SQL migrations in the repo, and the tests can run against in-process PGlite with no Docker. Schema is plain Postgres. Any Postgres host works. Auth Supabase Auth (email one-time code) for the admin and invited clients. A separate signed-cookie grant for passcode access. Passcode visitors should not need an account. Auth is isolated in src/server/auth/. Media storage Cloudflare R2, one public bucket and one private bucket, behind a MediaStorage interface Zero egress fees for full-resolution downloads. Interface has r2 and local drivers. Any S3-compatible store fits. Image processing Pre-generate derivatives with sharp in a CLI at upload time No per-request image transformation cost, predictable quality, and bulk shoots upload reliably from a laptop. Browser upload in the admin UI is a later phase using the same pipeline module. DNS Keep the domain registered at Squarespace, move nameservers to Cloudflare (free) R2 custom domains require the zone to be on Cloudflare. Records are documented, moving back is a nameserver change. Blog syndication Site is canonical (POSSE). GitHub Action cross-posts to Dev.to and Hashnode as drafts with canonical_url set. Medium, LinkedIn and Substack use their import tools manually. Those three have no usable publishing API today. Each target is an adapter file. Profile README Hand-written README.md with generated blocks between markers, checked for drift in CI Mark edits prose directly. Lists stay in sync with site content with no bot commits. Delete the markers and it is a static file. Lint and format Biome One fast tool. next lint no longer exists in Next 16. If the repo standards thread chose ESLint and Prettier, follow that instead. Tests Vitest for unit and integration, Playwright for end to end Standard for this stack. n/a Package manager pnpm, pinned through packageManager Fast, strict. n/a

docs.title: 3. Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  subgraph Repo["GitHub: markurtz/markurtz"]
    C["content/ (MDX, YAML)"]
    CFG["site.config.ts"]
    APP["src/ (Next.js app)"]
    RD["README.md (profile)"]
  end

  subgraph Vercel
    ST["Static pages: home, about, work, research, blog, projects, photos"]
    DYN["Dynamic routes: /clients, /admin, /api"]
  end

  subgraph Cloudflare
    DNS["DNS zone"]
    PUB["R2 public bucket, media.DOMAIN"]
    PRIV["R2 private bucket, presigned URLs only"]
  end

  subgraph Supabase
    PG["Postgres: galleries, photos, collections, gates"]
    AUTH["Auth: admin and invited clients"]
  end

  C --> ST
  CFG --> ST
  C --> RD
  APP --> ST
  APP --> DYN
  DYN --> PG
  DYN --> AUTH
  DYN -- "signs short-lived URLs" --> PRIV
  ST -- "img srcset" --> PUB
  CLI["scripts/photos CLI (laptop)"] --> PUB
  CLI --> PRIV
  CLI --> PG
  GA["GitHub Actions"] -- "syndicate posts" --> EXT["Dev.to, Hashnode"]
  DNS --> Vercel
  DNS --> PUB

Three properties drive the layout:

  1. Public content is static and lives in git. Blog posts, projects, papers and public albums are files. They build to static HTML, need no database, and the site works with every backend feature switched off.
  2. Private content is dynamic and lives in Postgres and R2. Client galleries change without a deploy and must never be in the static output or the client bundle.
  3. The browser never talks to the database. All reads and writes go through server components, server actions and route handlers that call a data access layer. Row Level Security is enabled on every table with no public policies, as a second line of defense rather than the primary one.

Rules the builder should encode in AGENTS.md:

  • Only src/lib/content/ imports from .velite. Pages call functions such as getPosts() and never touch the raw output.

  • The existing template pieces that do not apply to a website (Python packaging, PyPI publishing, MkDocs, the placeholder Dockerfile) are owned by the repo standards thread. This plan assumes they are removed or adapted there and does not depend on any of them.

docs.title: 6. Config-driven customization
docs.text: The aim is that routine changes are edits to site.config.ts, a content file, or theme.css, and never to a component.

docs.title: 6.1 site.config.ts
docs.text:
A single typed object, validated with Zod at build time so a typo fails the build with a clear message.

export const siteConfig = defineSiteConfig({
  url: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL ?? "http://localhost:3000",
  name: "Mark Kurtz",
  title: "Mark Kurtz",
  tagline: "TODO: one line",
  description: "TODO: two sentences used for SEO and the README",
  locale: "en-US",
  author: { name: "Mark Kurtz", email: "", avatar: "/avatar.jpg", location: "" },

  social: {                       // any subset, rendered in the footer, about page and README
    github: "markurtz",
    linkedin: "", scholar: "", orcid: "", bluesky: "", mastodon: "", x: "", email: "",
  },

  nav: [                          // order and labels of the header
    { label: "About", href: "/about" },
    { label: "Work", href: "/work" },
    { label: "Research", href: "/research" },
    { label: "Blog", href: "/blog" },
    { label: "Projects", href: "/projects" },
    { label: "Photos", href: "/photos" },
  ],

  projectCategories: [            // add a hobby by adding a line here
    { id: "software",    label: "Software",    icon: "code",   description: "" },
    { id: "3d-printing", label: "3D Printing", icon: "box",    description: "" },
    { id: "woodworking", label: "Woodworking", icon: "hammer", description: "" },
    { id: "diy",         label: "DIY",         icon: "wrench", description: "" },
  ],

  home: {                         // which sections appear on the home page, in order
    sections: ["hero", "featuredProjects", "latestPosts", "selectedPapers", "photoStrip"],
    counts: { featuredProjects: 4, latestPosts: 3, selectedPapers: 3 },
  },

  features: {                     // switch whole areas on or off
    blog: true, research: true, photos: true, search: true, contact: false,
    clientGalleries: false,       // also requires the backend env vars (§12.2)
    gatedPages: false,
    comments: false,              // giscus, backlog
    analytics: true,
  },

  blog: { postsPerPage: 10, showReadingTime: true, syndicationTargets: ["devto", "hashnode"] },
  media: { publicBaseUrl: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_MEDIA_URL ?? "", widths: [640, 1280, 2560] },
  clientArea: { label: "Client Galleries", defaultExpiryDays: 90, sessionDays: 30 },
});

src/lib/features.ts combines siteConfig.features with the presence of environment variables, so clientGalleries: true without database credentials renders a clear "not configured" page in development and fails the production build.

docs.title: 6.2 Adding content
docs.text: pnpm new post "Title", pnpm new project "Title" --category woodworking, pnpm new paper, and pnpm new album scaffold a file with valid front matter. Adding a new project category is one line in projectCategories. Its listing page, nav filter and README section follow from the config.

docs.title: 6.3 Theme
docs.text: src/styles/theme.css holds all design tokens as CSS variables under @theme for light and dark: colors, fonts, radius, content width. Fonts load through next/font in src/app/layout.tsx. Changing the look of the site is an edit to this one file.

docs.title: 7. Content model
docs.text: All collections are defined in velite.config.ts. Common fields on every collection: title, description, date, updated?, tags: string[], draft: boolean (excluded from production builds), featured: boolean, cover? (image, processed by Velite for dimensions and blur data), plus computed slug, url, readingTime and toc where there is a body.

docs.title: 7.1 Pages (content/pages/*.mdx)
docs.text: Free-form MDX for About, Hobbies, Uses and Now. The route reads the page by slug, so adding content/pages/reading.mdx plus a nav entry creates a new page with no code. The Hobbies page uses a <CategoryGrid /> MDX component that renders the configured project categories and the photos section, so it stays current as categories are added.

docs.title: 7.2 Data (content/data/*.yaml)
docs.text: experience.yaml (company, role, start, end, location, summary, highlights, links), education.yaml, and talks.yaml. The Work page renders a timeline from these. A print stylesheet on /work gives a clean one-page resume from the same data.

docs.title: 7.3 Blog (content/blog/)
docs.text:
---
title: "Post title"
description: "One or two sentences."
date: 2026-11-20
tags: [ml, compression]
cover: ./cover.jpg
draft: false
externalUrl:            # set this for posts hosted elsewhere. The card links out and no page is built.
externalSource:         # e.g. "Red Hat Developer", shown as a badge on the card
syndicate: [devto, hashnode]   # overrides blog.syndicationTargets, [] disables
canonicalUrl:           # only when this site is NOT the original home of the post
---

This covers both blog modes in the brief. Existing externally hosted posts are small files with externalUrl set, so they appear in the list, the feeds and the README immediately. Self-published posts have a body and get a page at /blog/[slug]. Syndicated copies are linked from the post footer ("Also published on") using the state file described in §11.

docs.title: 7.4 Papers (content/papers/*.mdx)
docs.text:
---
title: "Paper title"
authors: ["Mark Kurtz", "Coauthor Name"]
venue: "ICML"
year: 2026
date: 2026-07-01
type: conference        # conference | journal | preprint | workshop | thesis | patent | talk
links: { pdf: "", arxiv: "", doi: "", code: "", slides: "", video: "", poster: "" }
abstract: "…"
bibtex:                 # optional. Generated from the fields above when omitted.
featured: true
---
Optional plain-language summary in MDX. When present the paper gets its own page.

/research lists papers grouped by year with type filters, highlights the site author's name in the author list, and offers a copy-BibTeX button. Paper pages emit citation_* meta tags and ScholarlyArticle JSON-LD so Google Scholar and other indexers pick them up.

docs.title: 7.5 Projects (content/projects/<slug>/index.mdx)
docs.text:
One collection covers software, 3D printing, woodworking and DIY. The category field must match an id in siteConfig.projectCategories, and the build fails on an unknown category.

---
title: "Walnut standing desk"
description: "…"
date: 2026-05-01
category: woodworking
status: completed       # idea | in-progress | completed | archived
cover: ./cover.jpg
gallery: [./01.jpg, ./02.jpg]
links: { repo: "", demo: "", docs: "", printables: "", video: "" }
tech: []                # software: languages and frameworks
materials: []           # physical builds: [{ item, quantity, cost?, link? }]
tools: []
buildTime: ""           # e.g. "3 weekends"
difficulty:             # 1 to 5, optional
models: []              # .glb paths under /models for the 3D viewer
featured: true
---

Category-specific fields are all optional and the project page renders a section only when its data is present, so one template serves every category. For software projects with links.repo set, star count and primary language are fetched from the GitHub API at build time with a long revalidation window and a graceful fallback if the request fails.

docs.title: 7.6 Public albums (content/albums/<slug>/)
docs.text: index.mdx holds title, date, location, description, cover and optional travel notes as the body. photos.json is a manifest written by the photos CLI (§10.3) with one entry per photo: id, width, height, alt, caption, thumbhash and selected EXIF (camera, lens, focal length, aperture, shutter, ISO). The image files themselves are in the public R2 bucket, not in git. Albums have a kind of photography or travel so /photos can filter them.

docs.title: 7.7 MDX components
docs.text:
Registered once in src/components/mdx/index.tsx and available in every MDX file without imports:

Component Use Callout Notes, tips, warnings Figure Image with caption, zoom on click Gallery Grid of local images with the shared lightbox BeforeAfter Draggable comparison slider for builds and photo edits ModelViewer Interactive 3D preview of a .glb file, loaded only when scrolled into view BillOfMaterials Table from the project's materials front matter, with a cost total Steps Numbered build log steps GitHubRepo Repo card YouTube, Video Privacy-friendly lazy embeds CategoryGrid The configured project categories as cards Fenced code, math Shiki highlighting with titles and line highlights, KaTeX for $…$

Each component also exports a plain Markdown fallback used when a post is syndicated (§11.2).

docs.title: 8. Routes
docs.text:
Route Rendering Source / Static siteConfig.home plus featured content /about, /hobbies, /[page] Static content/pages /work Static content/data /research, /research/[slug] Static content/papers /blog, /blog/[slug], /blog/tags/[tag] Static content/blog /projects, /projects/category/[category], /projects/[slug] Static content/projects /photos, /photos/[album] Static content/albums plus public R2 /contact Static page, server action Resend, feature flagged /feed.xml, /atom.xml, /feed.json Static Blog, with full content for self-hosted posts /sitemap.xml, /robots.txt, /llms.txt Static Generated from content, excludes private routes /api/og Dynamic, cached Open Graph images per page /clients and below Dynamic, noindex Postgres plus private R2 /p/[key] Dynamic, noindex Gated MDX pages /admin and below Dynamic, noindex Admin only /api/health Dynamic Liveness plus one trivial database query

All static routes use generateStaticParams with dynamicParams = false so unknown slugs return a real 404.

docs.title: 9.1 Principals
docs.text:
Who How they authenticate What they can do Admin (Mark) Supabase Auth email one-time code. Email must be in ADMIN_EMAILS. Everything under /admin. Passcode visitor Enters a gallery passcode. No account. View that gallery, download if allowed, create and share collections if allowed. Invited client Supabase Auth email one-time code, invited by the admin to specific galleries. Public sign-up is disabled. Same as a passcode visitor, without typing a code, across all of their galleries at /clients. Share-link visitor Opens a collection share URL, optionally enters that collection's passcode. View, and download if allowed, only the photos in that collection.

Passcode is the default path because a client should be able to open a link from an email and be looking at photos in seconds. Accounts are optional and invite only.

docs.title: 9.2 Database schema
docs.text:
Drizzle schema in src/server/db/schema.ts, SQL migrations generated by drizzle-kit into src/server/db/migrations/. Row Level Security is enabled on every table with no policies for the anon or authenticated roles, so the Supabase public API exposes nothing. The server connects with the database connection string.

galleries
  id uuid pk, slug text unique, title, description, client_name, shoot_date date,
  cover_photo_id uuid null, status (draft | published | archived),
  passcode_hash text null, access_version int default 1,
  allow_downloads bool, allow_collections bool, expires_at timestamptz null,
  archive_key text null,            -- prebuilt zip of all originals
  created_at, updated_at

photos
  id uuid pk, gallery_id fk on delete cascade, filename, storage_prefix text,
  width int, height int, bytes bigint, content_type, taken_at timestamptz null,

A database constraint guarantees every row in collection_photos references a photo in the collection's own gallery, so a collection can never be used to reach photos outside it.

docs.title: 9.3 Passcode flow
docs.text:
1. The admin creates a gallery and either types a passcode or generates one (four random words). Only a salted scrypt hash from node:crypto is stored. The admin UI shows the passcode once, with a copyable link.
  2. The visitor opens /clients/g/<slug>. Without a valid grant they are sent to /clients/g/<slug>/unlock.
  3. The unlock server action checks the rate limit (5 failures per 15 minutes per hashed IP and gallery, stored in rate_limits), compares in constant time, records an access_events row, and on success adds a grant to the session cookie.
  4. The session is a JWT signed with GALLERY_SESSION_SECRET in a cookie named __Host-grants, with HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax and Path=/. Its payload is a list of grants: { kind: "gallery" | "collection" | "gate", id, v, exp }.
  5. Every request re-checks the grant against the database: the resource exists, is published, has not expired, and v equals the current access_version. Changing a passcode increments access_version, which revokes every outstanding session for that gallery immediately.

Unknown slugs and wrong passcodes return the same response so gallery names cannot be enumerated.

docs.title: 9.4 Authorization in one place
docs.text: src/server/auth/access.ts exports requireAdmin(), requireGalleryAccess(slug), requireCollectionAccess(token) and requireGate(key). Each returns the resource plus a capability object (canDownload, canManageCollections) or redirects. Every page, server action and route handler in the private area starts with one of these calls. The data access layer functions take the already-authorized resource id, and a unit test asserts that no file under src/app/(private) imports src/server/db directly.

docs.title: 9.5 Client collections and sharing
docs.text:
Inside a gallery with allow_collections on, the visitor can select photos (click, shift-click range, select all), then "Add to collection" to create a new one or append to an existing one. A built-in "Favorites" collection is created on first use so the heart button works with no setup.

Each collection has a share action that produces a URL of the form /clients/c/<token>. The token is 32 bytes of randomness, shown once and stored only as a SHA-256 hash. The creator can add an optional passcode, an expiry date, toggle downloads (never more permissive than the parent gallery), rename, reorder, remove photos, regenerate the link, or delete the collection.

Ownership: collections created by a signed-in client belong to that user. Collections created under a passcode session belong to the gallery, and anyone holding the gallery passcode can manage them, which matches how a couple or a family would share one code. The share page shows only the collection's photos and gives no route back into the full gallery. The admin sees every collection per gallery, which doubles as the client's selection list for retouching or prints.

docs.title: 9.6 Generic gated pages
docs.text: The same grant mechanism protects arbitrary content, which is the "passcode style pathways" requirement. An MDX file in content/private/ with gate: <key> in its front matter is served at /p/<key> only after requireGate(key) passes. These files are compiled by Velite into a separate server-only collection that is never included in generateStaticParams, feeds, sitemap or search. Because the repo is public, anything in content/private/ is still readable on GitHub, so this is for content that is unlisted rather than secret. Truly private text belongs in the database, and the gates table plus the admin UI leave room for a gated_documents table later.

docs.title: 9.7 Admin UI
docs.text: /admin is deliberately small: gallery list and create, gallery detail (settings, passcode, expiry, publish, member invites, photo order, cover selection, delete), the collections for a gallery, gates, and a recent access log. Photo upload in the first release is the CLI in §10.3. Browser upload is in the backlog and reuses the same pipeline module.

docs.title: 10.1 Buckets
docs.text: Bucket Access Contents PREFIX-public Public through the custom domain media.DOMAIN with long cache headers Public album derivatives only. No originals, GPS data stripped. PREFIX-private No public access. Reached only by presigned URLs created on the server. Client gallery originals and derivatives, zip archives.

docs.title: 10.2 Keys and derivatives
docs.text:
public:   albums/<albumSlug>/<photoId>/<width>.webp          widths from siteConfig.media.widths
private:  galleries/<galleryId>/<photoId>/original.<ext>
          galleries/<galleryId>/<photoId>/preview.webp        2560 px long edge, quality 85
          galleries/<galleryId>/<photoId>/thumb.webp          640 px long edge
          galleries/<galleryId>/archive.zip                   optional, all originals

Derivatives are sRGB, auto-rotated, with all metadata stripped. Originals are stored byte for byte. Photo ids are UUIDs, so keys are not guessable even in the public bucket.

docs.title: 10.3 Photos CLI
docs.text:
pnpm photos upload ./exports/smith-wedding --gallery smith-wedding     # private client gallery
pnpm photos upload ./exports/iceland --album iceland-2026              # public album
pnpm photos upload … --dry-run | --concurrency 6 | --archive

For each image the shared pipeline.ts reads dimensions and EXIF, computes a thumbhash, renders derivatives with sharp, uploads through the MediaStorage interface, then either inserts photos rows (client gallery) or writes content/albums/<slug>/photos.json (public album, committed to git). Uploads are idempotent by content hash, so re-running after a failure resumes. --archive builds and uploads the full-gallery zip.

docs.title: 10.4 MediaStorage interface
docs.text:
interface MediaStorage {
  put(key: string, body: Buffer | Readable, opts: { contentType: string; cacheControl?: string }): Promise<void>;
  signedGetUrl(key: string, opts: { expiresIn: number; downloadAs?: string }): Promise<string>;
  delete(keys: string[]): Promise<void>;
  exists(key: string): Promise<boolean>;
}

STORAGE_DRIVER=r2 uses the S3 client against the R2 endpoint. STORAGE_DRIVER=local writes under .data/media and serves through a development-only route with HMAC-signed URLs, so the whole client area runs and is tested on a laptop or in CI with no cloud account.

docs.title: 10.5 Delivery
docs.text:
• Public albums: a <Photo> component renders <img> with a srcset built from the pre-generated widths on media.DOMAIN, the thumbhash as a blur placeholder, and explicit width and height to prevent layout shift. It does not use the Vercel image optimizer, so there is no transformation cost.
  • Client galleries: after the access check, the server component signs thumb and preview URLs for the page (signing is a local HMAC, no network call) with a one hour expiry. Pages are paginated at 200 photos with infinite scroll through a server action.
  • Single download: GET /api/clients/download?photo=<id> re-checks access and canDownload, logs the event, and redirects to a five minute presigned URL with an attachment disposition. Bytes go from R2 to the browser, never through Vercel.
  • Download all: links to the prebuilt archive.zip when present.
  • Download a selection or collection: the browser streams a zip with client-zip from presigned URLs, which needs a CORS rule on the private bucket allowing GET from the site origin.

docs.title: 11.1 Publishing on the site
docs.text:
Write content/blog/my-post.mdx, open a PR (the Vercel preview shows the rendered post), merge. Drafts (draft: true) render in development and previews with a banner and are excluded from production, feeds and the sitemap. A future date schedules a post: it is excluded until a daily deploy hook rebuild picks it up.

Feeds: RSS, Atom and JSON Feed with full content for self-hosted posts and link-only entries for external ones. Feeds are the universal sync path, since Substack, Medium and newsletter tools can all import from a URL or feed.

docs.title: 11.2 Automated cross-posting
docs.text:
scripts/syndicate/ runs from .github/workflows/syndicate.yml, triggered on pushes to main that touch content/blog/** and by manual dispatch with a slug and a dry-run toggle.

  1. Collect posts that are not drafts, have no externalUrl, and list a target that has no entry yet in content/.syndication.json.
  2. Wait until the canonical URL on the live site returns 200, so the canonical link is valid before any copy exists.
  3. Transform the MDX to portable Markdown: remove imports, replace each custom component with its Markdown fallback (§7.7), rewrite relative image and link paths to absolute site URLs, and append "Originally published at ".
  4. Call each target adapter.
  5. Write the returned ids and URLs to content/.syndication.json and open a small PR with that change. The site reads this file to show "Also published on" links, and it is what makes the job idempotent.
    6. Target Method Canonical handling Default Dev.to REST API, DEVTO_API_KEY canonical_url field Created as a draft Hashnode GraphQL API, HASHNODE_TOKEN and publication id originalArticleURL Created as a draft Medium Manual, using Medium's "Import a story" with the post URL Medium sets the canonical link on import Documented step LinkedIn Manual article or link post Link back in the first line Documented step Substack Manual, or its RSS import Link back Documented step Bluesky, Mastodon Optional announce adapters that post the title and link n/a Off

    Cross-posts are created as drafts by default so Mark reviews formatting on each platform before publishing there. Setting syndication.autoPublish: true in the config changes that. Updates to an already syndicated post are not pushed automatically. The job prints which copies are now stale. Medium is manual because Medium no longer issues integration tokens for its publishing API, and LinkedIn and Substack have no article API.

docs.title: 12.1 Database and auth clients
docs.text:
• src/server/db/client.ts: a single postgres client using the Supabase transaction pooler URL with prepare: false and a small pool, wrapped by Drizzle.
  • src/server/auth/supabase.ts: @supabase/ssr server client bound to Next cookies, used only for Auth (sign in with a one-time code, read the verified user, admin invites with the secret key).
  • proxy.ts: refreshes the Supabase session cookie, with a matcher limited to /admin and /clients so the static site never runs it.
  • Supabase project settings: public sign-ups off, email one-time code on, custom SMTP through Resend (the built-in mailer is rate limited to a few messages an hour), site URL and redirect URLs set for production and Vercel previews.

docs.title: 12.2 Environment variables
docs.text:
Validated in src/lib/env.ts. Only NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL is required for the public site. The rest become required when the related feature flag is on. .env.example is rewritten to list exactly these.

Variable Scope Needed for NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL public Canonical URLs, feeds, Open Graph NEXT_PUBLIC_MEDIA_URL public Public album images DATABASE_URL server Drizzle (pooler URL) DATABASE_URL_DIRECT CI only Migrations NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY public Auth SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY server Admin invites ADMIN_EMAILS server Admin allowlist GALLERY_SESSION_SECRET server Grant cookie signing, 32 bytes or more IP_HASH_SALT server Hashing IPs in logs and rate limits STORAGE_DRIVER server r2 or local R2_ACCOUNT_ID, R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID, R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, R2_PUBLIC_BUCKET, R2_PRIVATE_BUCKET server and CLI Media RESEND_API_KEY, CONTACT_TO_EMAIL server Contact form GITHUB_TOKEN build, optional Higher rate limit for repo stats DEVTO_API_KEY, HASHNODE_TOKEN, HASHNODE_PUBLICATION_ID GitHub Actions secrets only Syndication

docs.title: 12.3 Keeping the free Supabase project awake
docs.text: Free Supabase projects pause after about a week without activity. A scheduled GitHub Action calls /api/health daily, which runs select 1. The same workflow doubles as an uptime check and fails loudly if the site or database is down. Upgrading to the paid tier removes the need for it.

docs.title: 13.1 Recommended setup
docs.text:
Keep the domain registered at Squarespace and point its nameservers at Cloudflare's free plan. This is required for the media.DOMAIN custom domain on R2 and gives one place to manage records.

  1. Add the domain as a site in Cloudflare (free plan). Cloudflare scans and imports the existing records. Check that any email records (MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC) were imported before continuing, because mail breaks if they are missed.
  2. In Squarespace, open the domain's DNS settings, turn off DNSSEC if it is on, and replace the nameservers with the two Cloudflare assigns. Propagation usually takes under an hour and can take up to a day.
  3. In Vercel, add the apex domain and www to the project under Settings, Domains. Vercel shows the exact records to create.
  4. In Cloudflare DNS, create those records with the proxy off (grey cloud, "DNS only"). Typically an A record on @ and a CNAME on www. Vercel issues the TLS certificates.
  5. In Vercel, set the apex as primary and www to redirect to it.
  6. In Cloudflare R2, connect media.DOMAIN to the public bucket. Cloudflare creates that record itself, proxied.
  7. For Resend, add the DKIM and SPF records it lists on a send subdomain.
  8. Any additional domains Mark owns can be added to the Vercel project as redirects to the primary.

docs.title: 13.2 Alternative without moving nameservers
docs.text: Add the Vercel A and CNAME records directly in Squarespace's custom DNS records. The site works, but R2 cannot serve from a custom domain. Public album images would then have to come from the rate-limited r2.dev address, which Cloudflare does not support for production. This is why §13.1 is the recommendation.

docs.title: 13.3 Deployments
docs.text: Vercel's Git integration builds a preview for every PR and production on merge to main. Environment variables are set per environment in Vercel. Database migrations run from a GitHub Actions workflow (db-migrate.yml) on changes under src/server/db/migrations/** on main, gated by a protected production environment so Mark approves each one.

docs.title: 13.4 Plan and cost caveats
docs.text:
Service Free tier fits? Notes Vercel Yes for a personal site The Hobby plan is for non-commercial use. Delivering paid client shoots through the site is arguably commercial, which would mean Pro at about $20 a month. Mark should decide this before promoting client galleries. Hosting on Cloudflare through OpenNext is the alternative with no such restriction. Supabase Yes Pauses when idle (§12.3). No automated backups on free, so a weekly pg_dump workflow that stores an encrypted artifact is in Phase 9. Pro is about $25 a month. Cloudflare R2 First 10 GB free About $0.015 per GB per month after that and no egress fee. 200 GB of shoots is roughly $3 a month. Cloudflare DNS Yes Resend Yes 3,000 emails a month on free.

R2 is delivery storage, not a backup. Originals should remain in Mark's own archive.

docs.title: 14. GitHub profile README
docs.text: Because the repo is markurtz/markurtz, GitHub renders the root README.md on Mark's profile page. The repo must be public and the file must be at the root. So the root README is written for profile visitors, and repository documentation lives in DEVELOPING.md and docs/, linked from one line at the bottom.

docs.title: 14.1 Structure
docs.text:
<picture> light and dark banner or wordmark from .github/profile/ </picture>

### Hi, I'm Mark

Two or three sentences: what I do, what I'm focused on now. (hand-written)

[Website](…) · [Blog](…) · [Research](…) · [LinkedIn](…) · [Scholar](…)
<!-- BEGIN:links --> … <!-- END:links -->

#### Featured projects
<!-- BEGIN:projects --> … <!-- END:projects -->

#### Latest writing
<!-- BEGIN:posts --> … <!-- END:posts -->

#### Selected publications
<!-- BEGIN:papers --> … <!-- END:papers -->

#### Beyond work
One line linking to woodworking, 3D printing and photography on the site. (hand-written)

<sub>This repo is also the source of my website. See DEVELOPING.md.</sub>

docs.title: 14.2 How it stays current and customizable
docs.text:
• Mark edits everything outside the markers directly in README.md. There is no separate template file to learn.
  • pnpm readme:generate (scripts/readme/generate.ts) rewrites only the text between BEGIN and END markers from the same content the site uses: featured projects, the newest posts including external ones, featured papers, and siteConfig.social. Counts and section order come from a readme block in site.config.ts. Removing a marker pair removes that section for good.
  • pnpm readme:check runs in CI and fails if the README is out of date, so the profile cannot drift from the site and no bot needs write access to main. A pre-commit hook runs the generator when content changes.
  • Links are absolute URLs to the live site. Output is deterministic, with no timestamps, so there are no noisy diffs.

docs.title: 14.3 Standards for the profile
docs.text:
• Short enough to read in one screen. Lists are capped at about five items.
  • Light and dark images through <picture> with prefers-color-scheme, stored in .github/profile/, each with alt text.
  • Only HTML that GitHub's sanitizer allows. No scripts, no inline styles.
  • No third-party stats or streak widgets by default. They depend on external services that are often down or rate limited, and they add no information a visitor needs. One can be added later as a hand-written line.
  • Set the repo's website field to the site URL and add topics, so the repo page links to the site.

docs.title: 15. Build phases
docs.text: Each phase is a mergeable increment that leaves main deployable. A phase is done when its acceptance criteria pass along with pnpm check (Biome, tsc --noEmit, unit tests) and pnpm build.

docs.title: Phase 0: Foundations
docs.text:
• Scaffold Next.js 16 at the repo root with TypeScript strict, Tailwind v4, Biome, Vitest and Playwright. Pin packageManager and add .nvmrc.
  • Add site.config.ts with defineSiteConfig and its Zod schema, src/lib/env.ts, src/lib/features.ts.
  • Rewrite .env.example, AGENTS.md commands and layout rules, and DEVELOPING.md for this stack. Coordinate with whatever the repo standards thread has landed rather than duplicating it.
  • CI on pull requests: install with a frozen lockfile, Biome, type check, unit tests, build. Reuse the existing reusable workflow files where they fit.
  • Scripts in package.json: dev, build, start, check, lint, format, typecheck, test, test:e2e, content, new, photos, readme:generate, readme:check, db:generate, db:migrate, db:studio.

Done when: a placeholder home page builds and CI is green.

docs.title: Phase 1: Design system and layout
docs.text:
• theme.css tokens, light and dark themes with next-themes, fonts through next/font.
  • Header with config-driven nav and a mobile menu, footer with social links, skip link, 404 and error pages.
  • shadcn primitives actually needed: button, card, badge, dialog, dropdown, input, tabs, tooltip, sheet.
  • Root metadata, Open Graph image route, favicon and manifest.

Done when: the shell is responsive from 320 px, keyboard navigable, and passes axe with no violations.

docs.title: Phase 2: Content engine and core pages
docs.text:
• velite.config.ts with all collections from §7, wired into next.config.ts so it runs in dev (watch) and build.
  • src/lib/content/ accessors: getPosts, getPost, getProjects, getProjectsByCategory, getPapers, getAlbums, getPage, getTags, with draft filtering.
  • MDX renderer and the components in §7.7.
  • Pages: home sections, about, hobbies, work, research, blog list with tags and pagination, post page with table of contents and previous and next links, projects list with category filter, project page, generic [page].
  • Feeds, sitemap, robots, llms.txt, JSON-LD (Person, WebSite, BlogPosting, ScholarlyArticle, CreativeWork, BreadcrumbList).
  • Search: build-time index and a command menu using MiniSearch.
  • pnpm new scaffolder.
  • Seed content: one real or clearly marked sample entry per collection and category, including one external blog post and one project with a 3D model, so every template is exercised. Mark the samples with TODO so they are easy to find and replace.

Done when: every route in §8's static list renders from content alone, an invalid front matter field fails the build with a readable error, and unit tests cover the accessors and schema edge cases.

docs.title: Phase 3: Profile README
docs.text:
• Replace the template README.md with the structure in §14.1, with placeholder prose marked TODO for Mark.
  • scripts/readme/generate.ts, readme:check in CI, banner images in .github/profile/.

Done when: running the generator twice produces no diff, and changing a featured project changes the README block.

docs.title: Phase 4: Public photography
docs.text:
• MediaStorage interface with local and r2 drivers.
  • scripts/photos pipeline and CLI for --album.
  • <Photo>, PhotoGrid and the lightbox, /photos and /photos/[album] with EXIF captions and keyboard navigation.
  • Sample album using the local driver with a few license-free images, so the pages build without R2.

Done when: an album uploaded with the CLI appears on the site with responsive images and blur placeholders, and Lighthouse reports no layout shift on the album page.

docs.title: Phase 5: Backend foundation
docs.text:
• Drizzle schema and first migration for all tables in §9.2, with Row Level Security enabled.
  • Database client, Supabase Auth server client, proxy.ts.
  • Passcode hashing, grant session cookie, rate limiter, access.ts guards.
  • /admin sign-in with one-time code and the allowlist, admin layout.
  • /api/health.
  • Integration test harness on PGlite that applies the real migrations.

Done when: the admin can sign in locally, the guards have unit tests for every allow and deny path including revoked and expired grants, and the public site still builds with all backend variables unset.

docs.title: Phase 6: Client galleries
docs.text:
• Admin: gallery create, edit, passcode set and rotate, publish, expiry, delete (which also deletes storage objects).
  • Photos CLI --gallery mode and --archive.
  • /clients landing (enter a code, or sign in), unlock page, gallery page with signed URLs, lightbox, single download, download all.
  • Access logging and the admin log view.
  • noindex headers, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer and Cache-Control: private, no-store on everything under (private).

Done when: a Playwright test covers wrong passcode, lockout, success, viewing, download, passcode rotation revoking the session, and expiry. A test confirms no storage key or other gallery's data appears in the page payload.

docs.title: Phase 7: Collections, sharing and client accounts
docs.text:
• Selection UI, favorites, create and edit collections, reorder.
  • Share links with optional passcode and expiry, /clients/c/[token], regenerate and revoke.
  • Selection and collection zip download in the browser.
  • Admin invites to galleries, /clients dashboard for signed-in clients, admin view of collections per gallery.

Done when: end to end tests show a passcode visitor creating a collection, a second browser opening the share link and seeing only those photos, and the link failing after revoke. An integration test proves a collection cannot include a photo from another gallery.

docs.title: Phase 8: Blog syndication
docs.text:
• Transformer with component fallbacks and absolute URLs, with snapshot tests.
  • Dev.to and Hashnode adapters, tested against recorded responses.
  • syndicate.yml with dry run, the state file, and "Also published on" links on posts.
  • docs/guides/writing.md covering the manual steps for Medium, LinkedIn and Substack.

Done when: a dry run prints the exact payloads for a sample post, and a second run after a simulated success does nothing.

docs.title: Phase 9: Hardening and launch
docs.text:
• Security headers in next.config.ts: HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, frame restrictions, and a Content Security Policy shipped in report-only mode first, then enforced.
  • Generic gated pages (§9.6) and the gates admin.
  • Contact form with Resend, a honeypot field and rate limiting.
  • Vercel Web Analytics and Speed Insights behind the feature flag. Both are cookieless, so no consent banner is needed.
  • Privacy page describing what the client area stores and for how long. Scheduled job that archives expired galleries.
  • Keep-alive and uptime workflow, weekly database backup workflow, Dependabot for npm and Actions.
  • Accessibility pass to WCAG 2.2 AA and a performance budget: Lighthouse 95 or higher on home, a post, and an album.
  • Guides in docs/guides/: customizing, writing, photos, client galleries, deploy and DNS.
  • Go-live checklist from §17.

docs.title: Backlog (designed for, not built)
docs.text: Item Where it attaches Browser upload in admin Presigned multipart upload to R2, then pipeline.ts in a server function Watermarked previews, proofing workflow, print orders New derivative in the pipeline, status column on collections Comments giscus component behind features.comments Newsletter RSS-to-email service pointed at /feed.xml Webmentions and social reply counts Section on the post page Travel map Album location coordinates on a map component Publication import from ORCID or Semantic Scholar Script that writes content/papers files Database-backed private documents gated_documents table next to gates Internationalization Not planned

docs.title: Guidance for the build thread
docs.text:
• Everything through Phase 9 can be implemented and tested without any cloud credentials: the content site is static, storage has the local driver, and database tests use PGlite. End to end tests for the client area need a real Postgres, so make them skip cleanly when DATABASE_URL is unset and run them in CI against a Postgres service container.
  • If the full plan is delivered as one diff, keep one commit per phase in the order above so the review can follow it.
  • Do not put Mark's real biography, employer history or publication list in from memory or guesswork. Use TODO placeholders and clearly labelled samples. Facts about Mark come from Mark.
  • Do not create cloud resources, change DNS, or add secrets. Those are in §17.

docs.title: 16. Quality standards
docs.text: Area Standard TypeScript strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, no any without a comment explaining why Server and client boundary Server components by default. "use client" only for interactivity. server-only on all of src/server. Input handling Every server action and route handler parses input with Zod and calls an access guard first Secrets Only in Vercel and GitHub encrypted settings. Nothing sensitive in NEXT_PUBLIC_*. Passcodes and tokens Stored only as hashes. Constant-time comparison. Rate limited. Tokens have at least 128 bits of entropy. Privacy IP addresses stored only as salted hashes. GPS data stripped from all derivatives. Private routes are noindex and no-store. Accessibility WCAG 2.2 AA. Semantic landmarks, visible focus, prefers-reduced-motion respected, alt text required by the content schema for cover images. Lightbox is fully keyboard operable. Performance Static by default, no client JavaScript for content that does not need it, explicit image dimensions, fonts self-hosted through next/font SEO Canonical URL on every page, Open Graph and Twitter cards, JSON-LD, sitemap, feeds linked from <head> Testing Unit tests for pure logic, integration tests for the data access layer and guards, end to end tests for the critical flows named in each phase Commits and PRs Conventional Commits, PR template from this repo, CI green before merge Dependencies Lockfile committed, Dependabot grouped weekly updates, no dependency added for something achievable in a few lines

docs.title: 17. What only Mark can do
docs.text:
None of these block building. They block going live.

  1. Confirm the primary domain and set NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL.
  2. Vercel: import the repo as a project, add environment variables, decide between Hobby and Pro (§13.4).
  3. Cloudflare: create an account, add the domain, switch nameservers at Squarespace (§13.1), create the two R2 buckets and an API token scoped to them, connect media.DOMAIN.
  4. Supabase: create a project, copy the connection strings and keys, turn off public sign-ups, set up Resend as SMTP.
  5. Resend: verify the sending domain.
  6. Syndication: create Dev.to and Hashnode API keys and add them as GitHub Actions secrets.
  7. GitHub: confirm the repo is public, add a production environment with required approval for migrations, set the repo website field.
  8. Content: replace the TODO placeholders in site.config.ts, README.md, content/pages/about.mdx and content/data/, and add real posts, papers and projects.

docs.title: 18. Risks and open questions
docs.text: Risk or question Default taken Revisit when Velite is pre-1.0 with a slow release cadence Use it, isolated behind src/lib/content/ A Next.js or TypeScript release breaks it. Switch to Content Collections. docs.text:
This folder is the complete written record of Mark Kurtz's personal site as decided up to 23 November 2026: what it is for, every page, the data behind it, how it is built and secured, and how it looks and moves. docs.title: Sources of truth, in order
docs.text:
When two sources disagree, the higher one wins.

  1. Mark's latest message on the point (recorded in the decision log).
  2. These documents.
  3. The static mock, v51 or later (sources). The mock is the visual and behavioural reference: its markup, CSS and scripts are the closest thing to production code.
  4. The "Mark Kurtz Site Structure" spec (Claude Doc). Its client-area section predates the 23 November switch to link-only access and is superseded there by 04-clients-sharing-embeds.md.
  5. The page-content finals (page-review/<page>/final.md), for exact copy.

docs.title: 10 · Content model
docs.text:
Status: Locked for structure (P6.1 to P6.5, 2026-11-21); field names are Default (derived from the mock's content/site.mjs, which is the working reference for every field below).

Public content is files in git. It builds to static HTML and needs no database. Private material is never in the repository (P6.4). Large media lives outside git and is uploaded with the CLI (P6.5).

docs.title: 1. Folders
docs.text:
A file's folder is its address. Each post, project or work is a folder with its text beside it. Repeated records are one YAML list per kind (P6.2).

content/
  labels.yaml                      sections, sub-sections, topics, regions, orgs
  site.yaml                        identity, menu, footer, profiles, stats (hand-kept part)
  pages/
    home.mdx                       hero, doors and row picks
    about.mdx  uses.yaml  colophon.mdx  privacy.mdx
  professional/
    index.mdx                      header copy, tiles, pinned picks
    experience.yaml                roles and education
    software.yaml                  repositories (public and not public)
    research.yaml                  papers and patents
    speaking.yaml                  talks, lectures, webinars, podcasts
  workshop/
    index.mdx                      header copy, tiles, featured, in-progress picks
    builds/<project>/index.mdx     one folder per project, photos.json beside it
    designs/<project>/index.mdx
    code/<project>/index.mdx
  studio/
    index.mdx                      header copy, favourites, "What I shoot with"
    <name-year>/index.mdx          one folder per work
    <name-year>/photos.json        written by the media CLI
  blog/
    external.yaml                  posts published elsewhere
    <slug>/index.mdx               hosted posts, images beside them
media/
  credits.json                     stand-in credits (must be empty at launch)

The compiled content is reached only through src/lib/content/ (architecture rule from PR #3).

docs.text:
content/labels.yaml is the single list of names. Every record's labels must exist here; the build fails otherwise.

sections:
  professional: { name: Professional, subs: { software: Software, research: Research, speaking: Speaking, experience: Experience } }
  workshop:     { name: Workshop,     subs: { builds: Builds, designs: Designs, code: Code } }
  studio:       { name: Studio,       subs: { photo: Photo, video: Video, travel: Travel, creative: Creative } }
regions:        [polar, europe, americas, africa-and-middle-east]
orgs:                                   # roles that items point to with `org`
  red-hat:      { name: Red Hat }
  neural-magic: { name: Neural Magic }
  burst:        { name: Burst, Inc. }
  personal:     { name: Personal }
topics:                                 # free tags; listed so spelling stays consistent
  [quantization, sparsity, speculative-decoding, benchmarking, agents, furniture, time-lapse, 3d-printing, plans, …]

Topics only filter (?topic=); there are no topic pages.

Field Type Required Notes id slug yes Unique per kind. For folder items it is the folder name. Used as the #anchor. title string yes Sentence case year int yes Places the item on the year rail. For repos, the start year. tags topic[] no org org id Professional only The role the work belongs to (P2.2) pin bool no Shows in the page's pinned band featured bool no Home picks and Speaking "Featured" size compact | standard | featured no Card size, default standard badge in-progress | coming-soon no Card badge (P1.3) tbd string[] no Field names that are Held (05) ask string no The open question for a held field unlisted bool no Readable by link, left out of lists, search, feeds, sitemap

docs.title: 4.7 Studio work (studio/<name-year>/index.mdx)
docs.text:
The folder name is the address: <name>-<year> (P3.3).

type Work = Shared & {
  place: string;                    // "Black Rock City, Nevada"
  area: string;                     // card line: "Nevada"
  region: Region;                   // filter
  start: string; end?: string;      // ISO dates; month and days derived
  shown?: string;                   // display override for the year, e.g. "2025–26"
  kinds: ("photo" | "video" | "travel" | "creative")[];
  lede: string;                     // "N days in <place>, <dates>."
  moment: string;                   // first-person opening of the story
  kit?: { camera?: string; lenses?: string; editedIn?: string };   // facts panel; defaults from uses.yaml
  film?: FilmRef;                   // leads the page in the cinema band and the mosaic
  photos: "photos.json";
};
// Body: story paragraphs, placed between photo rows with <Rows after={n} />.

type FilmRef = { key: MediaKey; duration: string /* "0:12" */; captions?: string /* .vtt key */; description?: string };

photos.json, written by the media CLI:

type Photo = {
  key: MediaKey;                    // "studio/iceland-2025/<uuid>"
  width: number; height: number;    // of the largest derivative
  takenAt: string;                  // capture time, drives the day-by-day rail
  alt: string;                      // required before launch
  caption?: string;
  thumbhash: string;
  focus?: [number, number];         // 0..1 focal point for crops (og:image, cards)
};

Item numbers on single-photo pages (/studio/<work>/<n>/) are the 1-based order in photos.json. Reordering photos changes those addresses, so the CLI appends and only reorders on request.

type Post = {
  title: string;
  hook: string;                     // one sentence: subtitle, card summary, meta description
  date: string; updated?: string;
  section: SectionId; sub: SubId; topics?: string[];

// Derived: readingMinutes, toc, wordCount.

type ExternalPost = {

  section: SectionId; sub: SubId; topics?: string[];
  source: "Red Hat Developer" | "Medium" | "Neural Magic" | "Reddit" | string;

docs.text:
type Uses = { updated: string; groups: { id: "desk" | "software" | "woodshop" | "3d-printing-and-electronics" | "camera-and-editing";
  name: string; items: { name: string; model: string; why: string; icon: IconName; url?: string; affiliate?: boolean }[] }[] };

The Camera and editing group is the source for Studio's "What I shoot with" and the default kit on works, so the three never drift.

docs.title: 5. Validation rules (build fails on any)
docs.text:
1. Every label, region and org exists in labels.yaml.
  2. Every built, pin and home pick resolves to an item.
  3. ids are unique per kind; folder names match ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$; Studio folders end in -<year>.
  4. Every photo has alt (production only), width, height and takenAt.
  5. No ⟦…⟧, [confirm or non-empty tbd remains (production only).
  6. No stand-in media key is referenced (production only).
  7. External URLs are https://.
  8. Home rows hold exactly four items each.

No content field. Build

docs.title: 11 · Database schema
docs.text:
Status: Default design implementing the Locked client model of 2026-11-23 (04). It replaces PR #3's galleries, gallery_members, collections, collection_photos and gates tables, and the structure spec's access_codes and share_links tables.

Postgres (Supabase), accessed server-side only through Drizzle. Row Level Security is enabled on every table with no policies for anon or authenticated, so the Supabase public API exposes nothing; the server connects with the database URL. Migrations are generated by drizzle-kit and committed with the schema change.

docs.title: 1. Entities
docs.text:
erDiagram

docs.title: 2. Tables
docs.text:
-- One delivered body of work: a shoot, a film, a set of files.
create table collections (
  id            text primary key,            -- short random id used in /clients/g/<id>/ (10 chars, base62)
  title         text not null,               -- "Smith wedding" (never in an address)
  kind          text not null default 'photo' check (kind in ('photo','film','mixed','files')),
  description   text,
  cover_item_id uuid,
  next_delivery text,                         -- "full reception, about Dec 5"
  status        text not null default 'draft' check (status in ('draft','live','archived')),
  archive_key   text,                         -- prebuilt zip of all originals, private bucket
  created_at    timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at    timestamptz not null default now()
);

-- A batch Mark delivers. Items carry the batch they arrived in, which drives "New".
create table deliveries (
  id            bigint generated always as identity primary key,
  collection_id text not null references collections(id) on delete cascade,
  seq           int  not null,               -- 1, 2, 3 per collection
  note          text,
  delivered_at  timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (collection_id, seq)
);

-- A photo, film or file.
create table items (
  id            uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  collection_id text not null references collections(id) on delete cascade,
  delivery_id   bigint references deliveries(id),
  kind          text not null check (kind in ('photo','film','file')),
  storage_prefix text not null,              -- private/collections/<cid>/<itemId>/
  filename      text not null,               -- original name, used for downloads
  width int, height int, duration_ms int, bytes bigint not null, content_type text not null,
  taken_at      timestamptz,                 -- capture time: timeline order and moments
  moment        text,                        -- "Ceremony"; groups the rail (else derived by time gaps)
  caption       text,
  alt           text,
  thumbhash     text,
  focus_x real, focus_y real,                -- 0..1, for preview crops
  sort_key      bigint not null,             -- taken_at order, ties by filename
  created_at    timestamptz not null default now()
);
create index items_collection_order on items (collection_id, sort_key);

-- Mark's tags in the five facets. "Delivery: New" is computed, not stored.
create table item_facets (
  item_id uuid not null references items(id) on delete cascade,
  facet   text not null check (facet in ('stage','where','people','type')),
  value   text not null,
  primary key (item_id, facet, value)
);

-- A link: Mark's root link for a collection, or a share made from another link.
create table links (
  id              text primary key,          -- random path id, 12 chars base62 (~71 bits); /s/<id>/
  parent_id       text references links(id) on delete cascade,   -- null = made by Mark
  collection_id   text not null references collections(id) on delete cascade,
  scope           text not null check (scope in ('collection','selection','filter','item')),
  filter          jsonb,                     -- scope='filter': {"stage":["Ceremony"],"people":["Family"]}
  item_id         uuid references items(id) on delete cascade,  -- scope='item'
  name            text not null,             -- "Family", "Photo 12"
  can_download    boolean not null default false,
  can_share_single boolean not null default false,
  can_make_shares boolean not null default false,
  show_preview    boolean not null default true,
  token_version   int not null default 1,    -- bump to invalidate every token ever issued for this link
  expires_at      timestamptz,               -- null = until turned off (P5.7)
  revoked_at      timestamptz,
  revoked_by      text,                      -- 'admin' or the link id that turned it off
  created_at      timestamptz not null default now(),
  last_opened_at  timestamptz,
  open_count      int not null default 0,
  last_seen_delivery int not null default 0, -- New badges: deliveries after this are new to this link
  check ((scope = 'item') = (item_id is not null)),
  check ((scope = 'filter') = (filter is not null))
);
create index links_parent on links (parent_id);
create index links_collection on links (collection_id);

-- Fixed selections (scope='selection').
create table link_items (
  link_id text not null references links(id) on delete cascade,
  item_id uuid not null references items(id) on delete cascade,
  sort    int  not null,
  primary key (link_id, item_id)
);

-- Audit trail. IPs are stored only as a keyed hash.
create table access_events (
  id         bigint generated always as identity primary key,
  at         timestamptz not null default now(),
  kind       text not null check (kind in ('open','open_fail','view','download','download_all',
                                           'link_create','link_turn_off','embed_view','preview')),
  link_id    text references links(id) on delete set null,
  item_id    uuid,
  ip_hash    text,
  user_agent text
);
create index access_events_link on access_events (link_id, at desc);

-- Contact form.
create table enquiries (
  id         bigint generated always as identity primary key,
  at         timestamptz not null default now(),
  name       text not null, email text not null, message text not null,
  source     text,                           -- page the popup was opened from
  ip_hash    text, spam_score real,
  handled_at timestamptz
);

-- Fixed-window counters, updated atomically (see 21 § rate limits).
create table rate_limits (
  key          text not null,                -- 'open:<ipHash>', 'open:<linkId>', 'contact:<ipHash>'
  window_start timestamptz not null,
  count        int not null,
  primary key (key, window_start)
);

Every table: alter table … enable row level security; with no policies.

docs.title: 3. Invariants
docs.text: # Invariant Enforced by I1 A child link belongs to the same collection as its parent Trigger links_same_collection on insert I2 A child link never allows more than its parent Trigger links_no_escalation (each can_* ≤ parent's) and the API I3 A child's items are within the parent's items API check at creation: selection ⊆ parent's effective items; filter = parent filter AND new filter; item ∈ parent's items I4 link_items.item_id and links.item_id are in links.collection_id Trigger I5 Turning off a link turns off its whole subtree revoked_at set on the link; effective state computed through ancestors (below), so descendants need no write I6 Mark's root links have no parent; client shares always do Check in the API; /clients/# addresses only for roots

docs.title: 4. Effective access
docs.text:
Access for a token is computed on every request from the link and its ancestors:

with recursive chain as (
  select l.*, 0 as depth from links l where l.id = $1
  union all
  select p.*, c.depth + 1 from links p join chain c on p.id = c.parent_id
)
select
  bool_and(revoked_at is null and (expires_at is null or expires_at > now())) as active,
  bool_and(can_download)     as can_download,
  bool_and(can_share_single) as can_share_single,
  bool_and(can_make_shares)  as can_make_shares
from chain;

The visible items are the root link's collection narrowed by each link's scope down the chain (selection, filter, single item), and only collections with status = 'live'. This query lives in one data-access function, resolveLink(id, tokenVersion), used by every client route (21).

docs.title: 5. "New" badges
docs.text: An item is New for a link when items.delivery_id's seq is greater than the link's last_seen_delivery. Opening the collection page with that link advances last_seen_delivery to the latest seq after the response is sent, so the badges show once.

docs.title: 6. Retention
docs.text: Data Kept Default access_events Rolling window 90 days (Held, F61); nightly job deletes older rows enquiries Until handled, then 1 year rate_limits Expired windows Deleted hourly Turned-off links Kept for the access log Until the collection is archived Archived collections Originals deleted from storage after 1 year (Default)

docs.title: 7. Backups
docs.text: Supabase daily backups (free tier: 7 days). docs.title: 4. The media CLI
docs.text:
One command for everything, run on Mark's laptop (scripts/media/, pnpm media …).

pnpm media upload ./exports/iceland --studio iceland-2025          # public Studio work
pnpm media upload ./exports/bench   --workshop builds/entryway-bench
pnpm media upload ./exports/smith   --collection k7Qm2xPa [--delivery "first look"]
pnpm media film   ./exports/iceland/film.mov --studio iceland-2025 [--captions film.vtt]
pnpm media og     --studio iceland-2025 [--item 3 --focus 0.4,0.3]   # recrop a preview
pnpm media talks                                                      # fetch and self-host talk thumbnails
pnpm media upload … --dry-run | --concurrency 6 | --archive

For each file the pipeline reads dimensions, capture time and EXIF; computes a ThumbHash; renders derivatives with sharp (films with ffmpeg); uploads through the MediaStorage interface (r2 or local driver); then either writes photos.json beside the content (public, committed to git) or inserts items rows and a deliveries row (private). Uploads are idempotent by content hash, so a re-run resumes. --archive builds the collection zip.

MediaStorage (from PR #3, unchanged): put, signedGetUrl, delete, exists.

docs.text: SVG first everywhere it works, plus favicon.ico. PNG only where required: apple-touch-icon (180), manifest icons (192, 512, maskable 512), and og:image/twitter:image banners (1200 × 630).
