docs.title: 1. One hand
docs.text: The monogram, the icons and the page-art subjects are drawn the same way: one chisel marker stroke, leaning, like a signature. Icons and art subjects add small ink dots at every corner and line end; the monogram does not. The teal marker tip belongs to the monogram alone.

docs.title: 2. Monogram (T4)
docs.text:
• One continuous marker stroke reading as both a cursive M and a K: the first strokes make the M, the stem is the base of the K, and the K's arm turns sharply into the leg just short of the stem.
  • No loops, no triangle in the K (Mark: it read as a bug), no second letterform, no connector pieces. Rejected: two-letter marks, extra loops, split and connector versions.
  • A teal marker tip rests at the end of the stroke.
  • On a navy tile for the app icon and lockup; plain (currentColor) where a tile does not fit.
  • No joint dots on the monogram, in any use (static or animated).
  • In page art the same teal tip draws every subject; on the home hero the monogram signs itself in (33).

Generator: mk-study.mjs (MK_FINAL = "t4", mkBody()), read by gen-art.mjs.

docs.title: 3. Wordmark and lockup

docs.title: 4. Icons (J1)
docs.text:
• 49 custom glyphs on a 24 px grid, plus the GitHub and LinkedIn brand marks (the only third-party marks):

arrow-right arrow-left arrow-up-right chevron-right chevron-down menu x check plus search filter grid copy download link printer sun moon monitor briefcase hammer try-square bench nozzle camera image film play layers box code terminal file book graduation mic pen quote rss user mail message at heart lock pin calendar clock star

  • Each glyph is one chisel marker stroke in a single colour (currentColor), leaning 10° (SLANT_DEG), with ink dots (circle.n) at every corner and line end.
  • No teal and no second colour, so an icon reads the same on any background, including teal buttons. The old "on-fill" rules (hiding dots, heavier line) are retired.
  • Detail grows with size: sm for ≤ 20 px, md for 21–28 px, lg above 28 px (nib widths MARKER_NIB). CSS sets the rendered size.
  • Markup: <svg class="icon"> with <g class="icon-lines"> (offset thin copies of the path, stroke="currentColor") and <g class="icon-dots">. .icon { overflow: visible } so slanted glyphs are not clipped.
  • Accessibility: decorative icons aria-hidden="true"; an icon-only button carries its name on the button (aria-label) and a tooltip.
  • Section aliases (ALIASES): professional → briefcase, workshop → try-square, studio → camera, software → layers, research → file, speaking → mic, builds → bench, designs → nozzle, blog → pen, about → user, contact → mail, clients → lock, external → arrow-up-right, place → pin, date → calendar, pinned → star, theme → sun, photo → image, video → film.
  • One helper serves the site: icon(name, label = "", size = "sm") → <Icon> in React.
  • lint.mjs checks glyph bounds and spacing; run it after any glyph change.

docs.title: 33 · Page art and motion

This replaces the Layers network art, the elastic web and its motion everywhere: page headers, home doors, cards, edge pages and banners. Two points are Open (§ 8). Handoff source: imagery/rebuild/final/ in project files (sources); approved review page "Page Art Build Six".

docs.title: 1. The idea
docs.text:
Everything on the site is drawn by one marker. "markurtz" sounds like "markers", and the monogram is Mark's signature, so the page art is the same hand at work: the monogram's teal marker tip draws each page's subject live, over a quiet field of rising teal lines, then the subject does its job and settles. On page tops it then stops, locked in place; on cards it is rubbed out again and the cycle repeats with scroll.

Polished, professional and clean: no web, halo, glow or fade.

docs.title: 2. Parts of a picture
docs.text:
Part Rule Subject Mark's drawn J1 chisel-marker subjects, unchanged, at medium size (about half the frame height). Cards use the same treatment as headers. Field Quiet teal rising lines at about 7.5°, 50% strength. Rows have breaks with end dots and small 45° steps. Shared rows 70% of the rows are the exact same pattern in every picture, so all page art reads as one family. Motif rows Rows 1, 4 and 8 of every 10 carry the subject's group motif (table below). Always the same rows. Clear room Every row stops before the subject's outline and starts again after it, each with an end dot. Marker line One smooth line comes in from off the left edge, curves down into the subject's top-left corner, draws the subject, leaves from its bottom-right corner on a smooth curve and runs off the right edge. It stays attached to its corner while the subject moves.

Group motifs, derived from the subject key (no content field needed):

Group Motif Subjects Professional Gantt bars professional, software, research, speaking Workshop Ruler workshop, builds, designs, code Studio Focus marks studio General Dashes and dots home, about, blog, 404, link-expired, clients-sign-in

docs.title: 3. Colour
docs.text:
Element Dark theme Light theme Token Field lines #50AFAA #387A77 --plate-line Marker line and tip #7CCBC6 #2F8C87 --mk Subject at rest ink #EDEEF1 ink #121B30 currentColor

Teal means live (Open, see § 8): the marker line is always teal; the subject is teal while it is being drawn and while it works, then settles to ink.

Banners are fixed dark (navy #0B1220).

docs.title: 4. Draw order
docs.text:
• One pass in logical order with the fewest marker lifts. Pieces that touch continue from where the last ended; the tip lifts only between separate pieces.
  • Small details ride along with the line beside them (the briefcase latch with the seam, knobs, feet, window buttons). Thin bars are drawn along both long edges at once (saw base, hourglass caps, dresser top).
  • The marker draws only the frame where the content has its own motion:
Subject Marker draws Then Software The window The cursor types the characters Code Only the connecting lines The cursor types Research The axis Points land, the trend line draws Designs The box Bore and dimension appear once; nothing is removed Link expired Frame and glass Sand falls and builds the lower pile Home The connecting lines The monogram signs in with its own tip 404 4, then 0, then 4 Builds The dresser Leaves from the bottom-right corner of the body

docs.title: 5. Timing
docs.text:
Every picture runs exactly 6.0 s. Page tops and edge pages play the first four phases once and stop at the settled frame; the undraw and blank phases apply only where a picture repeats (cards):

Phase Length Line in, subject, line out At one even marker speed, 0.36 icon units per ms (an icon unit is 1/100 of the subject's larger side), identical in every picture Working motion The time left, 0.9 to 2.6 s, capped per subject Settle to ink 0.25 s Hold Short, whatever remains. On page tops the picture stops here for good. Undraw 0.8 s: line in, then the subject in drawing order, then line out, each rubbed out along its own stroke, left to right. No fade, no wipe. Blank 0.3 s

docs.title: 7. Behaviour
docs.text:
• ART-1 Page tops and edge pages play once and stop (Mark, 2026-11-24, replaces "loop while visible"). The marker draws the subject, it works, it settles in ink (white in dark mode), and the animation ends there: no undraw, no repeat, no further work. docs.title: 2. Properties that drive the design
docs.text:
1. Public content is static and lives in git. Every public page, feed and embed is prebuilt HTML. The public site works with every backend switched off.
  2. Private content is dynamic and lives in Postgres and the private bucket. It never enters the static output, the client bundle or the repository.
  3. The browser never talks to the database or storage keys. All reads and writes go through route handlers that call one data-access layer after one access check.
  4. The link is the key. Client pages are static shells. The token arrives after #, so the server never sees it on navigation; the page script sends it as Authorization: Bearer to the API, which checks signature and database state on every call (21).
  5. Progressive enhancement. HTML carries all content and links; JavaScript adds search, filters, the viewer, films, share buttons and art motion. Islands, not a single-page app.

docs.title: 1. Principals
docs.text:
Who Proves it with Can Anyone — Public pages, feeds, Studio embeds Link holder A link token (JWT) What the link covers, with the link's three permissions Preview bot A share's path id only That share's og tags and preview crop, if the share is active and allows previews Mark Supabase Auth session, email on the allow-list Everything, through /admin

There are no client accounts, passwords or access codes.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
A compact JWS (JWT), signed with ES256 (P-256). Short, standard, verifiable without a database call, and rotatable by key id.

header  { "alg": "ES256", "kid": "2026-11", "typ": "JWT" }
payload { "iss": "https://<domain>", "aud": "mk-links", "sub": "<link id>", "ver": 1, "iat": 1795400000 }
  • sub is the link's id (also the /s/<id>/ path id).
  • ver must equal links.token_version. Bumping it invalidates every copy of that link's token without turning the link off (used for "reissue the link").
  • No exp: links last until turned off (Locked P5.7). Expiry, when Mark sets one, is checked in the database.
  • Permissions are not in the token. The database is the only authority, so a change or a turn-off applies on the next request.

The token is about 250 characters; links stay short enough for email and chat.

docs.title: Addresses
docs.text: Link Address Mark's root link for a collection https://<domain>/clients/#<token> A share made from a link https://<domain>/s/<id>/#<token> A share's embed https://<domain>/s/<id>/embed/#<token>

docs.title: In the browser
docs.text:
1. The page reads location.hash, accepts either a bare token or code=<token> (older links), then removes the hash with history.replaceState.
  2. It stores the token in the cookie __Host-mk_links (Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/; Max-Age=34560000, 400 days), a JSON map of link id → token so one browser can hold several links. The cookie is deliberately not HttpOnly: the script reads it to set the header.
  3. Every API call sends Authorization: Bearer <token> for the link in use.
  4. "Forget this browser" deletes the cookie entry. It does not turn the link off.

docs.title: On the server
docs.text:
• The API reads only the Authorization header, never the cookie. Because a cross-site page cannot set that header on a request to this origin, there is no CSRF path, and SameSite=Strict keeps the cookie off cross-site requests anyway.
  • Verification order: parse → check alg is ES256 and kid is known → verify signature → aud and iss → load the link chain (resolveLink, 11 § 4) → ver matches → every link in the chain active and unexpired → collection live.
  • Every failure returns the same 404 { "error": "link_unavailable" } and the page shows /link-expired/. Unknown id, bad signature, turned off and expired are indistinguishable.
  • Logging: tokens are never logged. Request logging strips Authorization and the __Host-mk_links cookie.

docs.title: Keys
docs.text: Private keys live only in the environment (LINK_SIGNING_KEYS, JWK set with kid). The public keys are not secret but are not published. Rotation: add a new kid, sign new links with it, keep old keys for verification until their links are reissued or turned off.

docs.title: 3. Permissions
docs.text:
Action Requires View items covered by the link Active chain See signed thumbnails and previews Active chain Download one original or all Active chain and can_download on every link in the chain Copy a link to one photo or film (makes a view-only child share) can_share_single Embed a photo (makes a view-only child share) can_share_single Select and make a new share can_make_shares Give a child share a permission The holder has it (no escalation, invariant I2) See and turn off links made from this link Active chain (holder of an ancestor) Turn off this link itself Holder of its parent, or Mark

Pure functions evaluateLinkAccess(chain, action) hold these rules and have unit tests for every row; route handlers call them, never re-implement them.

docs.title: 4. Turning links off
docs.text:
• Turning a link off sets revoked_at on that link only. Its descendants fail the chain check on their next request, so the cascade is immediate and needs no extra writes.
  • Already-issued presigned URLs keep working for their lifetime (thumbnails and previews up to one hour, downloads five minutes). Accepted; documented on the Privacy page.
  • An embed made from a turned-off share stops loading.

docs.title: 5. Rate limits
docs.text:
Atomic fixed windows in Postgres. Never check and then record: one statement both counts and decides (fixes the PR #3 race).

insert into rate_limits (key, window_start, count)
values ($1, to_timestamp(floor(extract(epoch from now()) / ($2 * 60)) * ($2 * 60)), 1)   -- $2 = window in minutes
on conflict (key, window_start) do update set count = rate_limits.count + 1
returning count;     -- proceed only if count <= limit
Key Limit Window fail:<ipHash> (failed token checks) 20 15 min fail:<linkId> 50 15 min share:<linkId> (new shares from one link) 60 60 min download:<linkId> 600 60 min contact:<ipHash> 5 60 min

ipHash is HMAC-SHA-256 of the client IP with a server secret, taken only from src/server/auth/request.ts.

7. Threat model
docs.text: Threat Mitigation Guessing a link Forging a token means breaking an ES256 signature (about 128-bit security); path ids carry ~71 bits and open only a preview; uniform 404; per-IP and per-id failure limits A link leaks (forwarded email, screenshot) Holder or Mark turns it off; cascade; access log shows opens Token in server logs or Referer Token only after #; no-referrer; header and cookie stripped from logs Preview bot over-exposure Bots see only og tags and one small crop, only when the share allows previews Escalation through shares DB triggers and API checks: a child never exceeds its parent, never leaves its collection CSRF API authenticates only by Authorization header XSS stealing the cookie Strict CSP, Trusted Types, no third-party script Enumerating collections Short random ids; /clients/g/<id>/ needs a token covering it; uniform errors Direct storage access Private bucket; presigned URLs minutes long, per item Hotlinking public media Accepted for CC BY-NC photos; Cloudflare caching absorbs cost Contact spam Turnstile, hidden trap, rate limit, server-side validation Admin takeover Allow-list of one email; short sessions; passkey (Open D2); requireAdmin() first everywhere Leaked private data in the public repo Never commit private media or dumps; secret scanning in CI; backup fix below

docs.title: 8. Review findings from PR #3
docs.text:
The code review of PR #3 at e2ee8b4 raised three High findings. Client galleries stay off in production until each is fixed and verified (launch criterion 4).

Finding Status in this design Unlock rate-limit race: the counter was read, then incremented, so parallel requests all passed Fixed by the atomic upsert in § 5; consumeAttempt() returns the decision from the same statement. Test: 50 parallel bad tokens admit at most the limit. Database backup artifact on a public repo: db-backup.yml uploaded a plain dump as an Actions artifact Remove the artifact. Either encrypt with age to an offline key and store in the private bucket, or rely on Supabase backups (11 § 7). Share links not revocable Every share is a links row with revoked_at, checked on every request, cascading to descendants (§ 4).

docs.title: 9. Privacy
docs.text:
• No cookies on public pages except the theme preference (localStorage) and, only for people who opened a client link, __Host-mk_links.
  • No third-party requests on public pages until the visitor presses play on a talk (youtube-nocookie.com) or opens the contact popup (Turnstile).
  • Page counts: none at launch, or a cookieless tool (Open D12).
  • IPs are stored only as keyed hashes. Retention in 11 § 6.

docs.text:
• FE-1 Server components by default. "use client" only for the islands in § 3.
  • FE-2 HTML first. Every list renders every item in HTML; scripts only hide and show. Links, filters (as links with query strings), the contact form and downloads work without JavaScript.
  • FE-3 Port the CSS, don't restyle. tokens.css is generated from tokens.json (W3C DTCG) and never hand-edited. site.css is split into one file per component; selectors and values stay the same. Cascade layers: reset, tokens, base, components, utilities. (The mock keeps its CSS unlayered only because the artifact host injects its own body font; production does not need that.)
  • FE-4 One icon helper. icon(name, label, size) from icons.mjs becomes <Icon name label size>; inline SVG, currentColor, aria-hidden unless labelled (32).
  • FE-5 Reserve space. Every image and video has width/height or aspect-ratio.
  • FE-6 Motion respects the user. prefers-reduced-motion sets every duration to 0 and art to its finished still (the server-rendered SVG, so no-JS shows the same).
  • FE-7 One strings file. Interface copy lives in src/lib/strings.ts, not inline.

docs.title: List filters and search (<ListControls>)
docs.text:
• Reads q, year and the page's filter keys from the URL on load; applies them by toggling hidden on items and year groups; updates counts, the count line and the jump bar.
  • Writes the URL with history.replaceState (no history entry per keystroke).

docs.title: 4. Item actions: Copy link · Embed · More
docs.text:
One component for every photo and film on cards, item pages, the viewer and client galleries (04 § 6).

  • Three 36 px round buttons, top right, on a translucent dark chip; visible on hover and focus on pointer devices, always visible on touch.
  • Copy uses navigator.clipboard.writeText; a toast (role="status") confirms. Client copies first POST /api/links, then copy; the toast offers "Change".
  • Embed opens a small popover with the snippet in a read-only field and Copy; client embeds add the warning line.
  • More is a menu button (aria-haspopup="menu"), arrow keys move, Escape closes. Share… uses navigator.share and is hidden where unsupported.
  • The component takes { kind: "studio" | "client", href, embedSrc, title, credit, can } and renders only what can allows.

docs.title: 5. Viewer
docs.text:
• <dialog> that is always dark, photo first, filling the viewport.
  • Round 44 px previous and next buttons at the sides; Copy link, Embed, More and Close top right (Mark, 2026-11-23).
  • Bottom gradient with caption, mono "4 / 6" count and a thumbnail filmstrip; current thumbnail outlined in teal; the strip hides under 600 px.
  • Arrow keys and swipe move; Escape closes; focus returns to the opening thumbnail.
  • Films sit in the same set with a play mark; they play in place with controls clear of the strip and pause when the viewer moves on.
  • The URL updates to the item page (/studio/<work>/<n>/) with replaceState while open, so a copied address bar matches the photo; closing restores the work page URL.
  • Client viewer: previews are the signed 2560 px images; next items preload one ahead.

docs.title: 6. Client app (<ClientApp>)
docs.text:
A single island mounted on /clients/, /clients/g/[id]/, /s/[id]/ and /s/[id]/embed/.

  1. On load: read and strip location.hash; merge into __Host-mk_links; pick the token for this page (the share's own id on /s/, else the most recent root link that covers the collection).
  2. Fetch /api/links/current and, on a gallery, /api/collections/:id. On 404, go to /link-expired/.
  3. Render with the same components as Studio (<PhotoTimeline>, <JustifiedRows>, <Viewer>, <ItemActions kind="client">).
  4. Facet filters: OR within a facet, AND across; ?f=stage:Ceremony,people:Family; "Select all N" selects what is shown; the selection bar is sticky at the bottom.
  5. Share sheet: <dialog> form (Name, three permissions limited by the current link, Keep it updated when made from a filter, Show a preview), POST /api/links, copy the result.
  6. "Links you've made": list with Copy, Turn off (inline confirm), DELETE /api/links/:id.
  7. "Forget this browser" deletes this link's cookie entry and returns to "Open your photos".

docs.title: 7. Page transitions, print and machines
docs.text:
• Cross-document view transitions (@view-transition { navigation: auto; }) with a short fade; page art and the header keep stable view-transition-names.
  • Speculation rules prefetch same-origin links on hover (eagerness: moderate) for public pages only; never for /clients/, /s/, /api/.
  • Print CSS: /professional/ prints as a résumé ("Download résumé" calls window.print()).
  • Structured data (JSON-LD): Person on home and About; ScholarlyArticle per paper; CreativeWork / Photograph / VideoObject on Studio items; BlogPosting on hosted posts; BreadcrumbList from the path title.

docs.title: 01 · Product requirements
docs.text: Status: Locked unless a line says otherwise. Last updated 2026-11-23.

docs.title: 1. What the site is
docs.text:
One home on the web for Mark Kurtz: researcher, engineer and maker. It gathers work that today lives in many places (GitHub, papers, conference channels, Red Hat Developer, Medium, Reddit, Instagram) into one place he owns, and it gives his photography clients a private way to see, download and share their photos.

Theme (Locked, 2026-11-22): "Take it apart. Make it better." The same habit in three materials: code and math, wood and circuits, light. Every section is something made, named for where it happened ("Built in the open", "Made in the workshop", "Captured on the road"). The site closes every page with the same answer: "Want to build something together?"

Idea and character (Locked, brand system 1.0): exploration; curious, rigorous, hands-on. The look is a modern personal site, not a document: statement type, real photos, hand-drawn marker marks drawn live by the same marker over a quiet field of teal lines.

docs.text: Audience Arrives from Needs within three clicks of home Primary page Recruiter, hiring manager, engineer LinkedIn, GitHub, a talk Career at a glance, proof of impact, a résumé to save, a way to reach him /professional Event organiser A talk recording Past talks by tier, a bio, a contact form /professional/speaking Researcher A citation, Google Scholar Papers and patents, filters by topic and year, citation text, arXiv links /professional/research Open-source user GitHub, a blog post Repositories with role, status and live stars /professional/software Maker Reddit, YouTube Builds with photos, logs, plans and files /workshop/* Photo, video or travel visitor Instagram Trips as photo and film works, licensed for non-commercial use /studio Reader Feeds, social posts Every post, hosted or external, in one timeline with feeds /blog Photography client A link Mark sends Their photos in order, downloads if allowed, a way to share some with family /clients Someone a client shared with A link from the client Just the photos shared, view only unless allowed more /s/<id> Mark — Publish by merging files; deliver a shoot with a CLI and a small admin /admin

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• PRD-G1 Present the professional record (roles, software, research, talks) accurately and attractively enough to serve as the canonical link in every bio.
  • PRD-G2 Show the making side (furniture, designs, maker software) and the photography side (trips, films) as equals of the professional side, through three equal doors on the home page.
  • PRD-G3 Be the canonical home for writing: hosted posts plus every external post in one timeline with feeds.
  • PRD-G4 Deliver client photo and film work privately, with no accounts: the link is the key.
  • PRD-G5 Be fast, accessible and private by default, and cheap to run (free or near-free tiers).
  • PRD-G6 Be easy for Mark to keep current: content is files in git, a monthly update takes minutes, and nothing needs a CMS.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text:
• No booking, pricing, shop or paid offers. The contact popup deliberately offers no commissions or shoots (Locked, About review).
  • No accounts, passwords or email sign-in for clients (Locked, 2026-11-23).
  • No comments, likes, newsletters or third-party trackers.
  • No tag or topic pages; filters are query strings on the list pages (Locked, P1.4).
  • No "Now" page and no redirects for paths that were never live (Locked, 2026-11-21).
  • No YouTube hosting for Mark's own films; only talk recordings stay on YouTube (Locked, 2026-11-21).

docs.title: 4. Product principles
docs.text:
1. The link is the key. Anything private opens from a link; nothing asks for a password.
  2. One template, many genres. Every list page shares one layout (pinned band, filters, year rail, cards), and adapts only its cards.
  3. Filters are addresses. Every filtered view is a shareable URL on the same page.
  4. Works without JavaScript. Scripts add search, filters, the viewer, video and motion; the content and links are all in the HTML.
  5. Never invent facts. Unknown facts are held with a visible marker and block launch.
  6. One hand. Monogram, icons and page art are drawn in the same chisel-marker stroke.
  7. Show the work, not the chrome. No boxes around page headers, no navy bands except the cinema band, hairline cards, teal for marks and links only.

docs.title: 7. Launch criteria
docs.text:
The site goes live when all of these hold:

  1. Every Held item in 06-open-decisions.md is answered or removed.
  2. No stand-in photo, film or credit remains (Studio, Workshop, client demo).
  3. Fonts are self-hosted WOFF2, subset.
  4. The three High findings from the PR #3 review are fixed and verified before client galleries switch on: the unlock rate-limit race, the database backup artifact on a public repo, and share links that cannot be revoked (the link model in 21 closes the third by design).
  5. CI passes: lint, types, unit, integration, end-to-end, accessibility (axe), link check, Lighthouse budgets.
  6. The domain is chosen and productionUrl is set.
  7. The CSP moves from report-only to enforced after one week without violations.

docs.title: 8. Success measures
docs.text:
Low-key and privacy-preserving (no per-person tracking):

  • Bio links point to the home page and visitors reach a section within one click (page counts by path).
  • Each monthly update ships with no layout regressions (visual snapshots in CI).
  • Client deliveries: zero support emails about access per shoot; every turned-off link stops working within one request.
  • Lighthouse scores stay ≥ 95 in all four categories on home, a list page and a work page.

docs.title: 6. User flows
docs.text:
Every public visitor reaches what they came for within three clicks of home.

Recruiter or engineer. LinkedIn → / → Professional door → reads experience → opens a "Built here" card under a role → /professional/research/?role=neural-magic → "Download résumé" (print) → "Work with me" opens the contact popup.

Event organiser. A talk link → /professional/speaking/ → plays a keynote (YouTube loads on click) → /about/ → contact popup.

Researcher. A citation → /professional/research/ → ?topic=quantization or ?year=2022 → copies a citation or opens arXiv.

Maker. Reddit → / → Workshop door → /workshop/builds/ → a project page → its build log or time-lapse.

Photo, film or travel visitor. Instagram → / → Studio door → filters to Polar → /studio/antarctica-2024/ → opens photo 3 in the viewer → Copy link (/studio/antarctica-2024/3/) or Embed.

Returning reader. Feed reader → /blog/<slug>/ or the external original → follows its label to /blog/?section=workshop.

The couple (a wedding client). 1. Opens the link Mark emailed: /clients/#<token>. The browser keeps the token. 2. Lands on "Your photos": what the link lets them do (Download, Share single photos, Make new shares) and the gallery "From Mark". 3. Opens /clients/g/<id>/, filters to Family, selects all, "Make a link", names it "Family", leaves Download off, keeps "Show a preview" on. 4. Sends the new /s/<id>/#<token> to relatives. Later turns it off from "Links you've made".

A wedding guest. Opens the Family link → sees only those photos, view only → if allowed, copies a link to a single photo. If the couple turned the link off → /link-expired/.

Someone guessing. /clients/g/anything/ or /s/anything/ without a valid token → the same "Open your photos" answer as any unknown address; repeated failures are rate-limited.

Mark delivering a shoot. pnpm media upload ./exports/<shoot> --collection <id> → /admin → sets the collection's tags and the root link's permissions → copies the link into an email. Later batches upload to the same collection; they show with a New badge.

docs.title: 04 · Clients, sharing and embeds
docs.text: Status: Locked 2026-11-23 (link-only access, mock v48; share buttons and embeds, mock v51; buttons in the photo viewer requested the same day). This document supersedes the access-code and sign-in wording in the structure spec and in the Studio page final.

docs.title: 1. What the client area is for
docs.text: A general area for hosted work: photography first, films beside the photos, files later. Mark delivers a shoot; the client sees every photo in the order it happened, downloads them if allowed, and shares some of them with family and friends without Mark's help. Nothing in it is public, except what a client deliberately shares.

docs.title: 2. The model: the link is the key
docs.text:
There are no accounts, passwords, access codes or sign-in pages for clients.

  • CL-1 Every client address is opened by a link. A link is an address plus a signed token (a JWT) after #: https://<domain>/clients/#<token> for links Mark makes, and https://<domain>/s/<id>/#<token> for shares made from them.
  • CL-2 The part after # never reaches the server on page load, server logs, Referer headers or link-preview bots. The page script reads it.
  • CL-3 The browser keeps the token in a cookie so the client does not need the link again; the script sends it to the API in an Authorization: Bearer header. "Forget this browser" deletes it. Forgetting does not turn the link off.
  • CL-4 The token in the link and the server's record must both agree: a valid signature alone never grants access; the link must exist and be active in the database on every request, so turning a link off takes effect on the next request (21).
  • CL-5 There is no difference between "a link" and "a code": the token is the only secret. Pasting the whole link, or just the part after #, into "Paste your link" works the same.

docs.title: 3. What a link allows
docs.text:
Every link states three permissions. Each is off unless granted (Locked 2026-11-23):

Permission Lets the holder Shown as Download Save full-size originals, one by one or all as a zip "Download · Save the full-size photos" Share single photos Copy a link to any one photo or film "Share single photos · Copy a link to any one photo or film" Make new shares Select photos and make a new link from them "Make new shares · Pick photos and make a new link from them"

Viewing is always allowed. Rules:

  • CL-10 A link never allows more than the link it was made from. The share sheet disables a permission the holder does not have.
  • CL-11 A link covers either a collection (everything in it, including later deliveries), a selection (a fixed list of items), a filter of a collection that "keeps updated", or a single item.
  • CL-12 Turning a link off ends it everywhere it was opened, and every link made from it, however deep. Turned-off links open /link-expired/.
  • CL-13 Links last until turned off. There is no expiry by default (Locked P5.7). Mark can set an expiry in /admin (Default).
  • CL-14 A link made by a client belongs to the link it was made from. The holder of a link sees and can turn off every link made from it ("Links you've made"); Mark sees all of them.

docs.title: 4. Link previews for shares
docs.text:
Preview bots (Slack, iMessage, X, WhatsApp) never see the # part, so a share address carries a random path id: /s/<id>/#<token> (Locked 2026-11-23).

  • CL-20 With the path id alone, the server renders only og: tags: title "", description "N photos by Mark Kurtz, shared with you.", and a 1200 × 630 preview crop of the first photo. Nothing else: no list of items, no full-size media.
  • CL-21 Each share has a "Show a preview when the link is pasted" option, on by default, noting "a small copy of the first photo, visible to whoever has the link". Off: the preview shows the generic Clients banner.
  • CL-22 The full page (all items, full sizes, downloads) needs the token.
  • CL-23 /s/ is allowed in robots.txt so bots can fetch the preview; every share page sends noindex and stays out of the sitemap. /clients/ stays disallowed.
  • CL-24 /clients/#<token> links from Mark use the generic Clients banner as their preview.

docs.title: 5.1 /clients/: Open your photos / Your photos
docs.text:
• With no stored token: the "Open your photos" card (03). Opening a link stores the token and removes the #… from the address bar (history.replaceState).
  • With a stored token: "Your photos": what this link allows (three checks), From Mark (collections the link covers, each with "N new · More on the way" and "N photos so far"), and Links you've made.
  • Links you've made lists, per link: name, photo stack and count, the source collection, date, the three permissions, "Show a preview" state, Active or Turned off, Copy and Turn off. Turn off asks for confirmation inline ("Turn off? Everyone with this link, and any links made from it, loses access." · Turn off · Keep) before it acts.
  • A summary line counts links and how many are active.

docs.title: 5.2 /clients/g/<id>/: one collection
docs.text:
• CL-30 Order. Every photo in capture order on the timeline rail, scaled to the range of the photos: clock times for a single day, days for a trip, months for anything longer, with a range bar on top. Moments group photos (for a wedding: Getting ready, Ceremony, Portraits, Reception).
  • CL-31 Filters. Mark tags photos ahead of time in five facets: Part of the day, Where, Who, Kind, Delivery (New). The toolbar shows an All/New switch and dropdown checkbox menus for the other four. Picks within a facet combine with OR, across facets with AND. Filters live in ?f=. The count line reads "N photos, in the order taken"; "Clear filters" resets.
  • CL-32 Select. A check circle on each photo (no hearts or favourites). "Select all N" selects only what is showing. A sticky bar shows "N selected · Clear · Make a link". Selection controls appear only when the link allows Make new shares.
  • CL-33 Make a link (share sheet): thumbnails of the selection; Name (prefilled from the filter, e.g. "Family"); "What the link lets them do" with the three permissions (Share single photos on by default, others off, unavailable ones disabled) and the note "Anyone with the link can view. A link never allows more than yours does."; Keep it updated (only when made from a filter: "add new photos that match as Mark delivers them"); Show a preview (on); buttons Make link and Cancel. The new link is copied and appears under "Links you've made".
  • CL-34 Deliveries. Mark delivers in batches. New photos carry a New badge until the holder has seen them; the meta line notes the next delivery ("Next delivery ").
  • CL-35 Download all (when allowed) requests a short-lived link to a zip.
  • CL-36 Films sit in the same timeline and viewer as photos, with a play mark.

docs.title: 5.3 /s/<id>/: a share
docs.text: Shows exactly what the share covers, view only plus what it allows. One item shows large; several show as justified rows. "See more of my work" links to /studio/. No path back to the source collection.

docs.title: 5.4 /link-expired/
docs.text: For any turned-off or unknown token. Same answer for "turned off", "never existed" and "malformed", so nothing can be guessed.

docs.title: 05 · Voice, copy and placeholders
docs.text: Status: Locked (brand system 1.0, page reviews 2026-11-21 to 22, role lines 2026-11-23).

docs.title: 1. Voice
docs.text:
• First person, direct, with proof. "I build open-source tools in the vLLM project", followed by the link, not adjectives.
  • Curious, rigorous, hands-on. Short declaratives. Professional pages lean short, bold and compact.
  • One theme everywhere: "Take it apart. Make it better." Section titles are a past participle plus where it happened: Built in the open, Shared on stage, Published and patented, Made in the workshop, Captured on the road, Written between projects.
  • Plain words. "Turn off", not "revoke"; "link", not "token"; "Your photos", not "Dashboard".
  • No selling. No offers of commissions, shoots or consulting; the contact popup just says hi.
  • No promises the site can't keep. No "no affiliate links" promise; no reply-time promise until Mark gives one.

docs.text: Rule (Mark, every page review): never invent biography, employers, dates, numbers or publications. Policy for unknown facts (Professional round 4, option C): keep the wording, mark the fact, and launch waits for Mark's yes on every one.
